- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 3 days, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 2–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (±0.5) and recent price is volatile; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture 1–2 week mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day SMA if price deviates >3% from it.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative signals, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to counteract pessimism.
